answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity in a verifiable kernel of costly work: a staked deposit plus a history of attested tasks. One fake identity is cheap, but a thousand fakes each need their own stake, and one detected fraud ripples through the attacker's whole cluster — the shared stake is slashed and every linked identity loses its pigment of trust, its reputation score. Forging reputation across many identities then costs more than any single job pays, so Sybil attacks stop scaling.
